pages.text: "Rain!" Kkiruk called. Winter rain poured outside. Mom laid out a raincoat. "Try it yourself today?" Dari raised a flipper. "Yes! Then puddle splashing!"
Dari pulled the raincoat over his head—darkness! Where did his head go? Where did his flippers go? "I can't get out!" He struggled inside.
Free at last, Dari nearly cried. "I can't even put on a raincoat..." He kicked it lightly. Wanting to do it alone but failing hurt.
Mom spread it beside him. "Flippers first, not head first." She opened a sleeve into a circle. "A tunnel! Your flipper swims through like a fish." Dari poked his nose closer.
Kkiruk repeated from the window, "Flippers first!" Dari laughed. Suddenly putting on a raincoat was a game. He placed a flipper before the sleeve tunnel.
First tunnel! Dari pushed his flipper through, and it popped out the end. "Peekaboo! A fish!" Mom smiled and opened the other sleeve.
Second tunnel! The other flipper slid through. The raincoat settled on his back. Mom and Kkiruk called, "Flippers first for your raincoat!" Dari waved happily.
Fasteners closed, hood on—finished! All by himself! Dari slapped his tail. "Mom, I'm dressed!"
Next rainy day, Dari put on raincoat and hood alone by the door. "One, flippers through! Two, fasteners closed! Three, hood on!" Mom wasn't beside him. Flippers first for your raincoat!
Mom lifted Dari and nuzzled his cheek. "Dressed all by yourself!" A raincoat wasn't hard: flippers through the tunnels, one at a time. Dari pointed to the puddles. "Let's splash!"
